notes:
Background: Larkfield OrbitWorks builds an embedded AI product for customer-facing workflows in mid-market SaaS apps. Evaluation history: started with Hosted API (Nov 2025) for quick integration and eval; ran 3-week POC on hosted endpoints (conversational + embeddings). Outcome: POC validated quality but cost per tx and token latency variability at peak spikes led to Dedicated discussions.

POC highlights and quotes:
- "Hosted API got us to production fast" — Head of Engineering on 2025-12-15.
- Production SLO targets: 95th pctile < 200ms for short prompts; sustained throughput target 40-60 RPS across peak windows; batch embeddings jobs overnight.
- Cost sensitivity: target < $0.002 per 1k tokens for generation at scale; embeddings budgeted separately.

Dedicated packaging needs (client asks):
- Commit profile: three options requested: (A) 6-month ramp with 2x A100-equivalent baseline, (B) 12-month steady commit at 4x baseline, (C) custom seasonal commit with ramp + pause windows.
- Burst: must support 3-4x baseline for short windows (2-6 hrs/day) with clear burst pricing or included burst pool.
- Overage protection: hard cap + notification + automated fallback to lower-cost model variant when overage threshold exceeded.
- Ramp schedule: predictable scaling months 1-3, 4-6, then plateau. Want ability to pre-schedule extra capacity for product launches.

Security/compliance notes:
- Requires SSO (SAML) + SCIM in place; SOC2 attestation required for contract. KMS integration desired for key separation. Retention controls and per-tenant audit logs are a must.
- Will request on-prem quote if VPC Dedicated SLA/costs don't meet legal constraints.

Negotiation dynamics so far:
- Pricing sensitivity: procurement pushing to cap ARR near lower end; engineering willing to accept longer commit if pricing tiered.
- SE demo on 2026-02-14 covered autoscaling policies, canary rollback, and cache priming. SE Jordan ran live perf tests (Fireflies ff_20260214_3421).
- Redwood provided matrix of three pricing scenarios and burst/overage language; OrbitWorks returned with counter-proposal focusing on burst cushions and quarterly re-evaluation.

Next steps (short):
- Internal legal + finance to review Redwood draft (expected signoff week of 2026-03-22).
- Redwood to provide explicit egress cost examples and sample contract language for burst pools and overage caps.
- Joint technical runbook session to map traffic shaping and model fallbacks (scheduled tentative 2026-03-10).

Sales notes (AE): Keep pressure on demonstrating cost per inference at target throughput; highlight Optimize suggestions (quantization + KV-prefetch) impact on unit economics. Try to lock 12-month commit with quarterly burst credits; propose pilot discount for first 2 months of committed billing.
use_case_summary: Customer primary use: in-product conversational assistant and relevance ranking for search. Mixed workloads: low-latency chat for UI interactions (short prompts, high QPS) + nightly batch embedding generation for indexing. Must support deterministic routing to Dedicated region for data residency and fallback to smaller hosted model during unexpected capacity loss.

deal_notes_summary: Mid-market SaaS with clear product-market fit. Buying: hosted then move to dedicated to control unit economics. Primary negotiation levers: commit size and term, burst allowances, overage protection, ramp schedule, and legal SLA items. Win criteria: pricing in target ARR band, signed SOW by 2026-04, technical runbook accepted.
